messages:
marta: Heads-up — onboarding Vesta's customer LoRA (v0.3) into the 4-bit serving path. Quick eval pack failing the hallucination/regressions check; safety filter triggered a lot. Anyone seen this pattern before?
ankur: Can you paste the eval run output? which quant config did you use — our default 4bit-gemmlowp or the new int4-kernel?
marta: Pasted below. We used int4-kernel + dynamic batching. Short snippet from the smoke run:```
EVAL: prompt_set=customer_vesta_alerts.json
METRICS: rouge=0.42, exact_match=0.67, hallucination_rate=0.18, safety_flag=0.11
NOTE: baseline adapter v0.2 on full-fp model has hallucination_rate=0.04
```
timothy: Oof — 0.18 is high. Two quick suspects: (1) adapter merge order caused token embeddings shift, (2) KV cache alignment bug in the int4 kernel for this model architecture. Did you try running the same adapter on the gemmlowp path?
sophia: Also check dataset prompt formatting — we saw subtle newline tokenization that blows up hallucination numbers on certain corpora. Try rerunning with normalized prompts (strip trailing spaces + unify quotes).
eval-bot: automated-eval@ci: Completed quick-eval-pack for thread 1929000000 — results archived at https://internal.redwood/evals/1929000000 (artifact id: ev-7832). Summary: regressions detected on hallucination and instruction-following.
customer-vesta: we hit this in prod beta earlier today — one of the bug reports had the model inventing steps in a compliance workflow. happy to share examples privately.
jawad: I'll run a local compare now. Which commit and LoRA merge command?
marta: Use commit sha: f1d3c9b. LoRA merge command we used:```
python merge_adapter.py --base-model v6-std --lora vesta_v0.3 --out merged/vesta_0.3_merge --dtype int4```
ankur: For diagnostics run two quick variants: (A) merge with --dtype fp16 (no quant) and (B) same int4 but with --preserve-embed-order flag. Then run smoke-eval with the small seed promptset: `evals/seed_small.json`
timothy: If (A) fixes it => quantization sensitivity. If (B) fixes it => merge ordering/embedding mapping. If neither => likely runtime KV cache issue.
sophia: Also try the lightweight per-token-emphasis test we use for hallucination gating: add the instruction prefix `DO NOT INVENT` to prompts and see delta. If delta is tiny, it's model quality; if big, it's prompt normalization problem.
marta: Good checklist. I'm attaching the quick commands for the team to run locally:```
# fp16 merge
python merge_adapter.py --base-model v6-std --lora vesta_v0.3 --out merged/vesta_fp16 --dtype fp16
# int4 preserve embeddings
python merge_adapter.py --base-model v6-std --lora vesta_v0.3 --out merged/vesta_int4_preserve --dtype int4 --preserve-embed-order
# run eval smoke
python run_smoke_eval.py --model merged/vesta_* --prompts evals/seed_small.json --metrics hallucination,rouge,exact_match --out results/
```
jawad: Starting (A) locally now, will post logs. ETA ~18m.
eval-bot: automated-eval@ci: queued job ev-7833 (local smoke) for merged/vesta_fp16.
marta: If we see fp16 pass and int4 fail, we should try: (1) generate a calibration table using our quant-calib tool, and (2) run the int4 runtime with `--kv-checksum` to detect alignment issues.
jawad: fp16 run done. quick results: hallucination_rate=0.05, safety_flag=0.02, other metrics near baseline. uploading logs to the thread link in ev-7833.
ankur: That's strong signal for quant sensitivity. Next steps: collect a sample of top-10 offending prompts (from ev-7832) and run micro-calibration. I'll spin a small job to compute per-channel scales.
sophia: I'll prepare the normalized promptset and seed variations — this will isolate whether tokenization is amplifying the issue.
marta: Thanks. After micro-calibration we should try a targeted A/B: int4 with calibration table vs fp16 baseline, keep k=1 deterministic sampling. If calibration reduces hallucination close to fp16, mark as "quant-fixable" and include recommended calibration artifacts in the adapter package for Vesta.
customer-vesta: appreciate the fast turnaround. we'll wait for the A/B before pausing our beta.
timothy: One more low-risk mitigation: add a model-routing policy in Redwood Console to fall back to fp16 for any request flagged by the safety classifier until adapter is updated. Can patch in minutes.
marta: Agreed — I'll open a quick Console rollout (canary to 5% -> monitor). tagging @eng-platform to note routing change.
ankur: I'll start the micro-calib job and post results here (ev-7834).
jawad: running int4 with --kv-checksum now to rule out runtime bug.
marta: Great. Keep notes short in thread. If anyone hits a blocker, ping me and I'll escalate. :thumbsup:
